title: EJ Swift wins the 2026 Arthur C Clarke award for science fiction

paragraphs.en: A novel about rewilding and climate activism in Britain has been named this year’s winner of the Arthur C Clarke award for science fiction.
paragraphs.zh: 一部关于英国生态修复和气候行动主义的小说被评选为今年亚瑟·C·克拉克科幻小说奖的得主。

paragraphs.en: When There Are Wolves Again by EJ Swift is an “ambitious study in the power of long-term hope in the face of climate breakdown”, said the award’s director, Tom Hunter.
paragraphs.zh: 该奖总监汤姆·亨特表示，EJ 斯威夫特的《当狼群再次出现》是“一部雄心勃勃的作品，探讨了面对气候崩溃时长期希望的力量”。

paragraphs.en: The award, now in its 40th year, is given each year to “the best science fiction novel” first published in the UK in the previous year. It was named after British author Arthur C Clarke , who gave a grant to establish the award in 1987. Swift receives £2,026 in prize money, in keeping with the award’s tradition of increasing it incrementally each year since 2001.
paragraphs.zh: 该奖已进入第 40 个年头，每年颁发给上一年度在英国首次出版的“最佳科幻小说”。它以英国作家亚瑟·C·克拉克命名，克拉克于 1987 年出资设立了这一奖项。斯威夫特获得 2026 英镑的奖金，这延续了该奖自 2001 年以来逐年递增奖金的传统。

paragraphs.en: When There Are Wolves Again follows two women across half a century in a near-future Britain. Lucy, whose childhood is shaped by the Covid lockdowns, becomes involved in climate activism and campaigns to revive Britain’s habitats, while Hester is a documentary-maker whose life was marked by the Chornobyl disaster. Their separate journeys eventually converge in 2070.
paragraphs.zh: 《当狼群再次出现》讲述了在近未来的英国，两位女性跨越半个世纪的人生故事。露西的童年被新冠疫情封锁塑造，她投身气候行动主义，致力于复兴英国的栖息地；赫斯特则是一名纪录片制作人，她的生命被切尔诺贝利灾难烙下印记。两人各自的人生旅程最终在 2070 年交汇。

paragraphs.en: This year, judges considered a record 132 books submitted by 52 UK publishing imprints and independent authors.
paragraphs.zh: 今年，评委们评审了创纪录的 132 本书，它们由 52 家英国出版品牌和独立作者提交。

paragraphs.en: In her Guardian review , Lisa Tuttle described the winning novel as “evocative and beautifully written”, praising it as a “character-driven … argument for rewilding in Britain”. Like Swift’s previous novel, The Coral Bones, she wrote, the book is “powered by a passionate love of nature and deep concern for the planet’s future”.
paragraphs.zh: 在《卫报》的评论中，丽莎·塔特尔称这部获奖小说“引人共鸣、文笔优美”，称赞它是“以人物驱动的……为英国生态修复辩护之作”。她写道，与斯威夫特此前的《珊瑚骨》一样，这本书“由对自然的炽热热爱和对地球未来的深切关切所驱动”。

paragraphs.en: Judging chair Dr Andrew M Butler, a critic and academic, called it “a story of environmental change and possible recovery”.
paragraphs.zh: 评委会主席、评论家和学者安德鲁·M·巴特勒博士称它是“一个关于环境变迁和可能复苏的故事”。

paragraphs.en: Hunter added: “Science fiction at its most powerful is often not about predicting the future but showing us that no one future has to be inevitable.”
paragraphs.zh: 亨特补充说：“科幻小说最有力量之处往往不在于预测未来，而在于向我们展示：没有哪一种未来是注定要发生的。”
